answer: Tie each agent to one DNA marker hash, taken at a lab. First, the lab reads 24 markers from a cheek swab and keeps only the hash. Second, the registry rejects any hash already on file, so one body anchors one identity, and the list stays public, a lantern peers check first. Third, the recheck runs on a quartz clock: each year a random agent gets 14 days for a fresh swab, and a miss freezes it. One test costs 99 dollars plus 150 in lab fees, so 1,000 fakes cost 249,000 dollars and need 1,000 real people in chairs. A fake is a sparrow in hawk feathers, and the flock spots it in seconds.
